issues.description: The term "LLMs" might not be immediately clear to all users, especially those new to the field of prompt engineering. While it's common in the AI community, it's jargon that could confuse some learners.
issues.recommendation: Provide a brief explanation of what "LLMs" stands for (Large Language Models) either in the title or in the introductory text. Alternatively, use the full term "Large Language Models" instead of the abbreviation.

issues.description: The quiz uses terms like "zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting" without providing immediate context or definitions. Users unfamiliar with these concepts might struggle to understand the quiz's purpose and questions.
issues.recommendation: Include brief definitions or explanations of "zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting" in the introductory text or as tooltips that appear when hovering over these terms. This will help users understand the context of the quiz.

issues.description: In question 2, once an answer is submitted, there is no way to go back and change the answer. This violates the user's control and freedom to correct mistakes or reconsider their responses.
issues.recommendation: Implement a 'Previous' button or allow users to revisit and modify their answers before finalizing the entire quiz. This would give users more control over their progress and reduce frustration.

issues.description: The 'Next' button changes color and shape between questions. After answering the first question, the button is a grey circle with the word 'Next'. After answering the second question, the button is a red circle with the word 'Next'.
issues.recommendation: Maintain a consistent button style (color, shape, and text) for the 'Next' button throughout the quiz to avoid user confusion. Choose a single, clear visual style and stick to it.

issues.description: The feedback messages after submitting an answer are inconsistent. For the first question, the feedback is 'Congratulations! You answered the question correctly.' For the second question, the feedback is 'The given answers are not correct.' followed by 'Correct Answer is:'.
issues.recommendation: Standardize the feedback messages to provide a consistent user experience. Use a consistent tone and format for both correct and incorrect answers. For example, always include a 'Correct Answer is:' section, even for correct answers.

issues.description: In question 2, the user can select incorrect answers without any immediate feedback or confirmation that they are making a mistake. This could lead to the user submitting an incorrect answer without realizing it.
issues.recommendation: Implement a real-time feedback mechanism that provides immediate visual cues (e.g., color-coding) when an answer is selected, indicating whether it's likely correct or incorrect. This will help users identify and correct errors before submitting.

issues.description: In question 3, the user can drag and drop the prompt parts in any order without any guidance on the correct sequence. This could lead to frustration and incorrect submissions.
issues.recommendation: Provide visual cues or hints to guide the user in arranging the prompt parts in the correct order. For example, use numbering or color-coding to indicate the expected sequence.

issues.description: In the third question, the user has to arrange the prompt parts to effectively apply few-shot prompting for writing event summaries. The user has to remember the order of the prompt parts to answer the question correctly. The user should be able to see the correct order of the prompt parts to answer the question correctly.
issues.recommendation: Provide a hint or example of the correct order of the prompt parts to help the user answer the question correctly. The user should be able to see the correct order of the prompt parts to answer the question correctly.

issues.description: There is no option to quickly navigate between questions. Users must click 'Next' or 'Back' buttons to move between questions, which can be inefficient, especially if they want to review or change answers on previous questions.
issues.recommendation: Implement a question navigation panel or a dropdown menu that allows users to directly jump to any question in the quiz. This would significantly improve the efficiency of use for experienced users who want to quickly review or modify their answers.

issues.description: The drag-and-drop interface for the third question lacks clear visual cues for successful placement. It's not immediately obvious that the items have been correctly arranged within the designated area.
issues.recommendation: Provide a clear visual confirmation when an item is successfully placed in the drag-and-drop area, such as a change in border color or a checkmark icon. This will improve the user's confidence and efficiency in completing the task.

issues.description: The large purple banner with the "Mastering Prompt Engineering for LLMs" graphic takes up a significant portion of the screen, especially on smaller displays. It doesn't add much value during the quiz itself and distracts from the questions.
issues.recommendation: Consider minimizing the banner during the quiz or moving it to a less prominent location, such as the top right corner. Alternatively, collapse the banner into a smaller icon that can be expanded if the user wants to see it.

issues.description: The progress bar is quite large and visually prominent. While it's useful to show progress, its size could be reduced to make it less distracting.
issues.recommendation: Reduce the height of the progress bar and use a more subtle color. The progress information is important, but it doesn't need to dominate the screen.

issues.description: After submitting an incorrect answer on question 2, the correct answers are displayed with a green background, and the incorrect answers are displayed with a red background. This is helpful, but the red and green backgrounds are quite intense and visually jarring.
issues.recommendation: Use softer shades of green and red for the background colors to indicate correct and incorrect answers. This will make the feedback less visually overwhelming.

heuristic: Help Recognize, Diagnose, Recover from Errors

issues.description: In question 2, when the user selects incorrect answers, the feedback only states "The given answers are not correct." and then provides the correct answers. This doesn't explain why the selected answers were wrong, hindering learning.
issues.recommendation: Provide more specific feedback explaining why the user's selected answers were incorrect. This could include a brief explanation of the concept or a reference to relevant material.

issues.description: The "i" icon next to the title "Mastering Prompt Engineering for LLMs" opens a popup with a brief description of the quiz. While this is helpful, it doesn't provide comprehensive help or documentation on prompt engineering concepts or how to best approach the quiz questions.
issues.recommendation: Link the "i" icon to a more detailed help page or documentation that explains the concepts being tested in the quiz, such as zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting. This could include examples and best practices.

issues.description: The platform provides feedback after each question, including the correct answer if the user answers incorrectly. However, it doesn't explain *why* the correct answer is correct, which limits the learning opportunity.
issues.recommendation: When providing feedback on incorrect answers, include a brief explanation of why the correct answer is the right choice. This will help users understand the underlying concepts and improve their knowledge.
